title: A landed item whose merge request waits no longer holds the files it pushed
goal: backlog.py held treats an item whose work commits are on a pushed code/<id> branch as holding no files, since it holds only its merge request, and held --overlaps names the pushed branch the next item rebases on; kb-sprint's run step says a session starts the next item on a hot file from that branch tip and lists the item whose merge request it waits for, so a merge-request wait does not idle the file.
notes: The failure it answers: most of a session's multi-hour wait on a hot file was a merge request waiting to merge, not work, because file-level held keeps an item's files until its code reaches main. Risk to test: the next item builds on unmerged code, so a failed merge request sends both back; the pushed branch is named so the rebase is deliberate. Workers already start from the orchestrator's branch tip, and ST-mf3byq2o gives each commit of a stacked branch its own Self-Reviewed trailer. It waits for the backlog.py split. Dropped: Operator's 2026-10-04 decision after the efficiency analysis: with one agent and no unattended runs this item has no measured pain
